question.problem:
| $x$ | $1$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $f(x)$ | $0.4$ | $0.25$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ | Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{128}$ be a random sample of size $n=128$ from a population with the probability mass function given above. Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is between $3.6$ and $4.2.$ *Hint: Two tables of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,0.7\,$ $\,0.7580\,$ $\,0.7611\,$ $\,0.7642\,$
$\,0.8\,$ $\,0.7881\,$ $\,0.7910\,$ $\,0.7939\,$
$\,0.9\,$ $\,0.8159\,$ $\,0.8186\,$ $\,0.8212\,$

$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,-1.7\,$ $\,0.0446\,$ $\,0.0436\,$ $\,0.0427\,$
$\,-1.6\,$ $\,0.0548\,$ $\,0.0537\,$ $\,0.0526\,$
$\,-1.5\,$ $\,0.0668\,$ $\,0.0655\,$ $\,0.0643\,$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
n=128,
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =1\cdot 0.4+4\cdot 0.25+6\cdot 0.1+8\cdot 0.25 \\  & =0.4+1+0.6+2 \\  & =4,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =({1}^{2}\cdot 0.4+{4}^{2}\cdot 0.25+{6}^{2}\cdot 0.1+{8}^{2}\cdot 0.25)-{4}^{2} \\  & =(0.4+4+3.6+16)-16 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(4,\frac{8}{128}) \\  & ∼N(4,0.0625).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(3.6<\overset{―}{X}<4.2).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3.6<\overset{―}{X}<4.2) & ≈-P(\frac{3.6-4}{\sqrt{0.0625}}<Z<\frac{4.2-4}{\sqrt{0.0625}}) \\  & ≈-P(-1.6<Z<0.8) \\  & =P(Z<0.8)-P(Z<-1.6) \\  & =Φ(0.8)-Φ(-1.6).\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.8)=0.7881, \\ Φ(-1.6)=0.0548.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3.6<\overset{―}{X}<4.2) & =Φ(0.8)-Φ(-1.6) \\  & =0.7881-0.0548 \\  & =0.7333.\end{aligned}
$$
